name: Jotham (son of Uzziah)
title: The Righteous King of Judah
summary: Jotham was king of Judah and the son of King Uzziah (Azariah). He first ruled as co-regent while his father was afflicted with leprosy, and then as sole king. He did what was right in the Lord's eyes and strengthened Judah militarily and economically, but the people continued their corrupt practices.

keyEvents.title: Co-regent during his father's illness
keyEvents.description: When King Uzziah was struck with leprosy for burning incense in the temple, Jotham took charge of the king's house and judged the people in the land.

keyEvents.title: Building projects in Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: Jotham built the upper gate of the Lord's house and carried out extensive construction work on the Ophel wall in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Fortresses and Towers in Judah
keyEvents.description: He built cities in the hill country of Judah and constructed forts and towers in the wooded areas to strengthen the country's defenses.

keyEvents.title: Victory over the Ammonites
keyEvents.description: Jotham waged war against the king of the Ammonites and defeated them. The Ammonites were forced to pay him a substantial annual tribute of silver, wheat, and barley for three years.

keyEvents.title: Walked Steadfastly Before the Lord
keyEvents.description: Jotham became powerful because he walked steadfastly before the Lord his God, even though he did not enter the temple of the Lord as his father had done.

keyEvents.title: Time of the Prophets' Ministry
keyEvents.description: During Jotham's reign, the prophets Isaiah, Hosea, and Micah were active, proclaiming God's word to Judah and Israel.
